points.title: Proposition and truth value
points.must: Proposition = statement that is true or false; represented by a variable with value 1 (true) or 0 (false); only two truth values.
points.model: Proposition = a statement that is either true or false (e.g. 'the door is open'). Represented by a Boolean variable A, B, C… Truth value = 1 (true) or 0 (false) — only two values. Computers use two states because high/low voltage (transistor on/off) is easy to tell apart and reliable.

points.title: Logic gate and truth table
points.must: Logic gate = electronic component performing a Boolean operation on binary inputs with one binary output; truth table = all input combinations with the output; n inputs → 2ⁿ rows.
points.model: Logic gate = electronic component that performs a Boolean operation on one or more binary inputs and gives a single binary output. Truth table = table listing every possible combination of inputs and the output for each. n inputs → 2ⁿ rows.

points.title: Switch model of AND and OR
points.must: AND = switches in series (both closed); OR = switches in parallel (at least one closed).
points.model: AND = two switches in series: lamp on only if A and B are both closed. OR = two switches in parallel: lamp on if A or B (or both) closed. NOT = normally-closed switch: pressing it (1) turns the lamp off (0).

points.title: NOT, AND, OR
points.must: Meaning, notation (¬A/Ā, A·B, A+B) and symbol shape of each.
points.model: NOT: one input, output is the opposite; X = ¬A (Ā); triangle + bubble. AND: 1 only when all inputs are 1; X = A · B; D shape (straight back). OR: 1 when at least one input is 1 (inclusive, both = 1 too); X = A + B; curved back, pointed front.

points.title: NAND, NOR, XOR
points.must: Meaning, notation and symbol of each.
points.model: NAND = NOT AND: 0 only when all inputs are 1; X = ¬(A · B); AND shape + bubble. NOR = NOT OR: 1 only when all inputs are 0; X = ¬(A + B); OR shape + bubble. XOR: 1 when inputs are different; X = A ⊕ B; OR shape with an extra curved line at the back.

points.title: Truth tables of the two-input gates
points.must: Complete table for AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR.

points.title: Identifying a gate from its table
points.must: Rules: 1 only on 11 → AND; 0 only on 00 → OR; 0 only on 11 → NAND; 1 only on 00 → NOR; 0110 → XOR.
points.model: Output 1 only on (1,1) → AND. Output 0 only on (0,0) → OR. Output 0 only on (1,1) → NAND. Output 1 only on (0,0) → NOR. Outputs 0,1,1,0 → XOR. Multi-input XOR = 1 when an odd number of inputs are 1.

points.title: Universal gates
points.must: Definition; NAND and NOR are universal; NOT, AND, OR from NAND.
points.model: Universal gate = gate from which any other gate / any circuit can be built: NAND and NOR. NOT = A NAND A. AND = (A NAND B) NAND (A NAND B). OR = (A NAND A) NAND (B NAND B) = ¬(¬A · ¬B) = A + B. With NOR: NOT = A NOR A. Used because one cell type is cheaper to manufacture.

points.title: Notation and the NOT bar
points.must: Different notations; a long bar over a group acts as brackets.
points.model: NOT: ¬A, Ā, A′. AND: A · B, AB, A ∧ B. OR: A + B, A ∨ B. XOR: A ⊕ B. A bar over A · B = ¬(A · B) (NAND) is NOT the same as ¬A · ¬B.

points.title: Rows and row order
points.must: 2ⁿ rows; binary counting order; column pattern.
points.model: n inputs → 2ⁿ rows (3 → 8, 4 → 16, 5 → 32). Order = binary counting 000, 001, … 111. Last column alternates every row, middle every 2 rows, first every 4 rows.

points.title: Order of precedence
points.model: Order: brackets → NOT → AND → OR. A + B · ¬C = A + (B · (¬C)), not (A + B) · ¬C. Put XOR in brackets.

points.title: Truth table with intermediate columns
points.must: Method and an example such as X = (A + B) · ¬C.
points.model: Method: 2ⁿ rows, inputs in binary order, one column per operation (inner first), then output. X = (A + B) · ¬C: output for rows 000–111 = 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0.

points.title: From words to an expression
points.must: Key words → operators; brackets; greenhouse / turnstile example.
points.model: and/both → AND; or/either/at least one → OR; not/is off → NOT; exactly one/different → XOR; neither…nor → NOR. Greenhouse fan: hot (T) and window closed, or humidity high (H): F = T · ¬W + H. Turnstile: valid card and (school hours or staff): O = C · (H + S).
